candidates.exact_span: The known uses of the receiving water(s) Segment 20.6.4.98 are livestock watering, wildlife habitat, marginal warmwater aquatic life and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification of the receiving segment determines which water quality criteria (e.g., warmwater vs marginal warmwater) govern numeric limit selection and applicability for parameters such as pH.

candidates.exact_span: The known uses of Segment 20.6.4.99 are warmwater aquatic life, livestock watering, wildlife habitat, and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If Segment 20.6.4.99 rather than 20.6.4.98 is the operative receiving segment, the applicable aquatic-life use category (warmwater vs marginal warmwater) and thus the governing numeric criteria could differ.

candidates.exact_span: The designated uses of Animas River, in both Section 20.6.4.403 and 404 NMAC, are coolwater aquatic life, irrigation, livestock watering, wildlife habitat, public water supply, industrial water supply and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether Animas River designated uses (coolwater aquatic life, irrigation, etc.) supersede or combine with Segment 20.6.4.98/99 known uses could change which WQS criteria and numeric limits are selected for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The limiting pH numeric criteria in 20.6.4.900 NMAC for primary contact and warmwater, marginal warmwater and coolwater aquatic life designated uses are pH within the range of 6.6 to 9.0 standard units (su).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage states the enforceable numeric pH range and ties it to specific designated uses; different readings of which uses apply would change whether this 6.6–9.0 limit is the operative comparison value.

candidates.exact_span: The site-specific pH standard of 6.6 – 9.0 is established at the end-of-pipe.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the limit is applied at end-of-pipe versus another location (e.g., in-stream) affects which reported measurements are compared against the enforceable numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: The NMIP requires site-specific pH standard to be applied at end-of-pipe for all dischargers.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of NMIP applicability could confirm or alter the measurement location for pH limit comparison, changing which data points are evaluated for exceedance.

candidates.exact_span: The limitation and monitoring requirements for pH of 6.6 to 9 are continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether 'continued in the draft permit' establishes an enforceable numeric limit and an ongoing monitoring obligation for FY2025, versus report-only or non-operative draft language, would change both limit applicability (A) and monitoring requirement status (B).

candidates.exact_span: if a discharge poses the reasonable potential to cause an in-stream excursion above a water quality criterion, the permit must contain an effluent limit for that pollutant.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This reasonable-potential trigger governs whether toxics effluent limits are required at all; different interpretations of 'reasonable potential' would change whether enforceable numeric toxics limits exist for comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The facility is a minor industrial with the highest monthly average flow over the most recent 24-months as 0.177 MGD (0.274 cfs).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Effluent flow (Qe) is an input to reasonable-potential and dilution calculations; a different interpretation of the stated flow value or its relevance would change derived limit values or whether limits are imposed.

candidates.exact_span: For industrial facilities, the highest monthly average flow over the most recent 24-months is used for reasonable potential calculations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The flow-averaging methodology determines Qe used in reasonable-potential analysis; alternative interpretations of which months or averages count could change whether reasonable potential is found and thus whether toxics limits apply.

candidates.exact_span: The facility discharges to an irrigation ditch. Water only flows in the ditch when the fields need water. The rest of the year the ditch is dry, 4Q3 is 0.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Intermittent discharge and 4Q3=0 affect receiving-flow (FQa) in dilution/reasonable-potential calculations (A), whether monitoring is required during dry or no-flow periods (B), and whether periods qualify as documented no-discharge versus unresolved missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: No samples have been taken of the ditch water when flowing and there are no ambient data.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Absence of effluent and ambient data affects whether reasonable-potential/toxics limits can be established or must remain unresolved (A), and whether missing results reflect documented no-data conditions versus inadequate evidence of required monitoring (C).

The critical dilution formula directly governs derivation of water quality-based effluent limits; interpretation of CD inputs—especially FQa when 4Q3 is stated as 0—could change computed limit values or leave applicability unresolved.
